    Know the difference

    Plywood or block board?

    Plywood

    Layered for all-round strength

    Thin hardwood veneers glued at right angles. Strong in every direction, holds screws firmly and is the first choice for carcasses, kitchens and wardrobes.

    See plywood     Block board

    Solid core for long spans

    Solid timber strips between veneers. Lighter and very stiff along its length, so it suits doors, long shelves, beds and table tops that must not sag.

    Buying block boards in Kakinada

    Block board
    questions.

    For homeowners, carpenters, interior designers, architects and builders. Still unsure? Call or WhatsApp us and we will help you choose.

    What is a block board?
    A block board has a core of solid timber strips between veneer faces. It is lighter than plywood of the same thickness and resists sagging, so it suits doors, long shelves, beds and table tops.
    Should I use block board or plywood?
    Use block board where a piece spans a long width and must stay straight, such as doors, long shelves and table tops. Use plywood for carcasses, kitchens and wardrobes, where all-round strength and screw holding matter most. Tell us your design and we will suggest the right mix.
    Which thickness do I need, 19 mm or 25 mm?
    19 mm suits doors, long shelves, wardrobe shutters and tables. 25 mm is for table tops, beds, large doors and long-span shelving, where rigidity is critical.
